title: Burnham says he was not aware of Brand's 'horrific' crimes
description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said Russell Brand has rightly been held to account for his "horrific" crimes and sought to explain Labour's previous
body: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said Russell Brand has rightly been held to account for his "horrific" crimes and sought to explain Labour's previous association with the comedian.Brand was found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault on Thursday.Some within the Labour Party attempted to court Brand's support more than a decade ago, before police began investigating him.Speaking on Friday, Burnham said: "It's not always the case that people know everything about people in public life."Ed Miliband, then the Labour leader, was interviewed by Brand in the run-up to the 2015 general election.In 2014, Burnham, then the shadow health secretary, posted on Twitter in support of Brand following allegations about the comedian's housing arrangements.It is not clear what Burnham had been referring to in his 2014 tweet, but the previous day, The Sun claimed Brand had paid rent at a property owned by a landlord in a tax haven, while at the same time campaigning against tax avoidance.Brand threatened to sue the newspaper and said he would give the money to victims of the Hillsborough disaster, a group Burnham has long campaigned for.At the time, Burnam said it was "depressing to see media mission to discredit someone who stops playing their game" and urged Brand to "keep going".Asked about that social media post on Friday, Burnham told the BBC "all I can say is I had no idea of the full extent of what he was doing or what he went on to do".The PM added: "His [Brand's] crimes are horrific, he's rightly been held to account, justice for the victims and that is the right course that's been taken here."It's not always the case that people know everything about people in public life, but what is important is that where there is wrongdoing it is exposed."The prime minister added: "Credit to the victims, huge credit, the courage that it's taken, but also the journalists who've exposed this."Brand was found not guilty of two other counts of rape, and one count of attempted indecent assault.During a four-week trial, Brand faced allegations from six women spanning the decade between 1999 and 2009.The 51-year-old was refused bail and will spend the weekend in custody before he is due to return to the same court on Monday for sentencing.

schema.headline: Burnham says he was not aware of Brand's 'horrific' crimes

title: Austrian police investigate man for leaving 17-year-old on Germany's highest mountain Zugspitze
description: The weather was so poor that the two climbers were soon knee-deep in snow, according to Austrian reports, and their plans to reach the 2,962m summit s
body: The weather was so poor that the two climbers were soon knee-deep in snow, according to Austrian reports, and their plans to reach the 2,962m summit soon changed.At one point they separated and the 21-year-old descended alone. The reason they split is unclear, and a police spokesperson declined to comment, citing the ongoing investigation.Seven mountain rescuers responded to the call, and a helicopter eventually airlifted the teenager off the mountain. She was then taken to hospital by ambulance.Although the teenager survived, what happened on Zugspitze on Sunday is reminiscent of a fatal incident on Austria's highest peak, the Grossglockner, in January 2025.A 33-year-old woman froze to death on the Grossglockner after her boyfriend left her on the mountain, and he was later found guilty of grossly negligent manslaughter.The boyfriend had insisted he had left her there while trying to get help, telling the court he had loved his girlfriend and that he was deeply sorry.The case reverberated throughout the mountaineering community at the time, with prosecutors arguing that as the more experienced climber, he was the responsible guide on the trip and had failed to turn back or call for help in time. In the latest case in Austria, police have said once they have completed their investigation, a report will be sent to Innsbruck public prosecutors, who will decide if a criminal offence has been committed.

schema.headline: Austrian police investigate man for leaving 17-year-old on Germany's highest mountain Zugspitze

title: Childminder who left more than 20 children alone in her home jailed
description: Figure caption, Childminder who left more than 20 children alone at home jailedByBen PhilipReporting fromat Kirkcaldy Sheriff Court and James DelaneyB
body: Figure caption, Childminder who left more than 20 children alone at home jailedByBen PhilipReporting fromat Kirkcaldy Sheriff Court and James DelaneyBBC ScotlandUpdated 1 hour agoA childminder who admitted leaving children she was caring for alone and unsupervised in her home has been jailed for two years.More than 20 unattended children, two under the age of one, were in Amanda Mathewson's house in Dunfermline, Fife, when she was arrested in August 2024.Her offending only came to light after concerned parents spied on her leaving for a school run without their children.An internal Care Inspectorate probe found Mathewson, who was been licensed to look after eight children under the age of 16 at any one time, had been tipped off about inspections by an unknown staff member.Mathewson previously pled guilty to wilfully neglecting, abandoning and exposing children in a manner likely to cause them unnecessary suffering or injury to their health.Sheriff John MacRitchie said Mathewson had committed a "gross abuse of a position of trust" during sentencing at Kirkcaldy Sheriff Court.He read victim impact statements from parents of affected children who described them suffering from "nightmares and anxiety" and developing a "distrust of childcare providers".Mathewson had been a self-employed childminder for 30 years prior to her arrest.An unannounced visit by the Care Inspectorate in August 2023 rated areas including care, learning and the setting as "very good", praising her "warmth, kindness and nurturing approach".But a year later, one couple became suspicious that all was not as it seemed.A friend had mentioned their two children, aged one and three, were not with Mathewson when she was on a school run.BBC Scotland News has spoken to the father of the children. He has not been named to protect their identity.The couple watched Mathewson in secret on 26 August 2024, parking opposite her home when their two boys were meant to be in her care as she went to collect other children from a local primary school.They saw Mathewson leave the home with two young girls in a pushchair, then went to the front door - where the father said a child could be heard "screaming" inside.The couple walked through a side gate to get to the back garden where they found a number of unsupervised children playing.'Slumped to the floor'Image source, SuppliedImage caption, Amanda Mathewson spent 30 years as a self-employed childminderThey were able to enter the property through the back door, finding a child "lying under a table" crying in severe distress.Upstairs, the father said "a dozen or so young children" were sitting on the floor of a spare bedroom, with another on a double bed, as a TV on top of a chest of drawers loudly played a children's programme.He said two others were "tightly strapped into a buggy in a way it was not meant to be used"."It was August. It was a particularly warm summer. It was hot in that room," he said."There was no food, no water, no toys, no activities for the children to be engaged in."The father said he was cradling two of the children in his arms as he walked downstairs when Mathewson returned home.He described her reaction to seeing him as being "like her soul had left her body"."I'll never forget it, she was like a child caught in the act of doing something they shouldn't be doing," he said."She took her jacket off and she just slumped to the floor. I asked her; 'Amanda, what the hell? How many laws have you broken here?'""It's obvious to us now. Her entire life was a lie. She has fabricated pretty much her entire life, her entire personality. It just crumbled in an instant."'Military operation'Mathewson was arrested and charged a short time later. When police arrived at the home, she had 15 children aged under 12 in her care, as well as 10 children under primary school age and two children under the age of one.During the subsequent investigation, various children told their parents that being left alone in Mathewson's home was commonplace.Parents also raised concerns that their children had not eaten or had anything to drink during her care.Some also reported their children returning home in dirty nappies.A court hearing was later told how Mathewson would play loud music and prevented parents from coming into her home in an attempt to hide her offending.Another parent told BBC Scotland News his daughter was "rummaging in a food waste bin" at nursery after spending mornings at Mathewson's home.For months after her arrest, he said his daughter would become "distraught" whenever they drove past her house.He said it became "really difficult" for the family to travel from one side of the town to the other without her becoming distressed."I can't imagine what must be going through her mind, the fear of going back there," he said."That was heartbreaking and we didn't know what to do or how to help."He described Mathewson's system of avoiding parents bumping into each other at the same time as being like a "military operation"."We were let down. We were lied to. Our children were neglected," he said."The only question I have is; Why?"Image caption, One parent told BBC Scotland his daughter became "distraught" whenever they drove near Mathewson's homeThe Care Inspectorate's August 2023 visit was meant to be unannounced, but the regulator has since admitted it is likely Mathewson received "confidential information" about inspections from an employee.The insider is yet to be identified, despite an internal investigation.A spokesperson for the Care Inspectorate said Mathewson "broke the trust" of families.They said "inspection, complaints and conflict of interest procedures" had been updated in following feedback from affected parents.Maria Lloyd, independent chairwoman of the Fife child protection committee, said a "learning review" would take place in the wake of the case.She said it would consider whether improvements to "practice, processes or partnership working" were required.A Scottish government spokesperson said the Care Inspectorate had carried out an audit of the way complaints against Mathewson were handled.They added: "We know Scotland's childminding community will be deeply distressed by this case."We are working with the independent regulators to strengthen practice, improve processes and enhance transparency."Law firm Irwin Mitchell Scotland - who are representing a number of families involved -  said they have been instructed to explore a civil case against the Care Inspectorate.Partner Kim Leslie said: "It is beggars belief that a failing of this magnitude could go unnoticed. "This is a fundamental breach of trust which, by the regulator's own admission, completely compromised the efficacy of regulatory scrutiny. "The parents want the Care Inspectorate to be held to account."

schema.headline: Childminder who left more than 20 children alone in her home jailed

title: Katherine Ryan says she feels 'grief and relief' after Russell Brand conviction
description: Speaking about the guilty verdict of his trial, on the latest episode of her podcast Telling Everybody Everything, Ryan said: "It really made me feel
body: Speaking about the guilty verdict of his trial, on the latest episode of her podcast Telling Everybody Everything, Ryan said: "It really made me feel just quite dysregulated again, caught off-guard, emotional, in awe of the survivors who also had nothing to gain."They came forward despite Russell Brand having fame, power, money, and a legion of fans ready to attack them."She added: "I will never be someone who like, dances on graves. There has been some justice done today. There's a level of relief, but there's grief alongside relief."Everything's nuanced, and it was proved in court that a terrible thing happened, and that means that a terrible thing happened."I just think again and again about people who have been hurt, and who have to carry that, who've carried that around long enough, and will continue to carry that in some way, regardless of what justice is done."Brand is now also being investigated over further rape allegations made by two women, police have now said.Details in legal documents from a hearing at London's Southwark Crown Court before Brand's criminal trial began suggest that one of the women was 16 years old at the time and featured in a Channel 4 documentary.Brand was accused by four women of rape, sexual assaults and emotional abuse in a joint Channel 4 Dispatches, Times and Sunday Times investigation in September 2023.The actor and comedian denied the allegations.None of the women who featured in the media investigation were the complainants from Brand's criminal trial.On Thursday it emerged that Brand was facing further rape allegations made by two women. The Metropolitan police said he had previously been interviewed under caution in relation to them.During a pre-trial hearing in October Brand tried unsuccessfully to have his criminal case thrown out.His lawyers argued that the actor and entertainer couldn't receive a fair trial because of the publicity following the Dispatches programme.Prosecutors opposed Brand's application to have his case stopped.It was during that hearing that the prosecution said one of the complaints made in the documentary was being investigated.Riel Karmy-Jones KC said: "Of the four women in the Ch4 documentary, two concern events outside the jurisdiction."One did not disclose any offence. The other is being investigated."There had been some interaction in 2018, she did not report the matter until 2024, after the documentary was aired."In documents submitted to the court for the hearing prosecutors also said it was "plainly incorrect" to say there had been a decision not to investigate."The outstanding charges against RB in respect of 'Alice' from Dispatches demonstrate that there has been no such decision – rather that the police will and have responded appropriately once a formal allegation is made."The head of the Metropolitan Police has said he "wouldn't be surprised" if more people came forward to make allegations about Russell Brand.Sir Mark Rowley also told BBC Radio 4's Today programme on Friday that what he heard reported from Brand's trial at Southwark Crown Court came very close to "victim blaming".

schema.headline: Katherine Ryan says she feels 'grief and relief' after Russell Brand conviction

title: US midterm results spark fears in Israel over future of two countries' ties
description: As the US midterm election results rolled in, long-held Israeli assumptions about the transatlantic alliance began to shatter."For us in Israel, this
body: As the US midterm election results rolled in, long-held Israeli assumptions about the transatlantic alliance began to shatter."For us in Israel, this will be a generational sea change," wrote one prominent journalist in Israel's biggest-selling newspaper, right-leaning Yedioth Ahronoth. "The [prime minister, Benjamin] Netanyahu government sowed the wind and reaped the tsunami."Israel's opposition leaders have lined up to blame their prime minister, with one saying the US results showed "just how toxic Netanyahu has become" among both Democrats and Republicans.The prime minister himself has so far remained silent."Israel's political establishment understood intellectually that things have been shifting. They have not understood how much and how quickly," one US official with knowledge of the situation told me.Israel's relationship with the US was a campaign issue in races across America.Many Democratic candidates were sharply critical of Israel's actions in Gaza and the occupied West Bank, and the costs of the joint US-Israeli war on Iran was a key issue for many voters.The US president himself blamed the Iran War for the Republican rout – a war that Israel's leader is widely seen as having promoted to him.And US Vice-President JD Vance cited the US relationship to Israel as one of four key reasons voters had deserted the party, hammering home the message that the relationship is now seen as a political problem by its key ally."That might be even worse than what happened in the midterms," Israeli political and security analyst Yaakov Katz told me. "Because the Democrats we knew about, now [Vance] is pointing the finger and saying: 'Our voters want us to change our position on Israel' – and Israelis don't fully understand where this is going."The question plaguing Israelis now is what this means for Israel's security and influence.The sense of staunch US military and diplomatic support had remained unshaken in Israel despite growing anger among US voters, President Donald Trump's public insults to Netanyahu, and differences over Israel's actions in Iran and Lebanon.Israel's prime minister continually boasted of his closeness to Trump, describing his "true friendship" and "unwavering support".And just nine months ago, Israelis watched their armed forces wage war on Iran hand in hand with the US military, as the "unprecedented" coordination of the two allies became a daily mantra among military spokespeople and politicians.So Trump's unexpected statement during a Fox News interview this week that he would stop $3.8bn (3.4bn euros; £2.8bn) in US military aid to Israel two years earlier than planned, caused shock here – not so much for the loss of aid as for what the move said about Israel's status as a diplomatic partner.Israel's president said the announcement came as "a bolt from the blue"."Nobody knows anything," was the headline in a report by Yedioth Ahronoth, adding that officials were still struggling to understand whether Trump's remark was serious, two days on.The Israeli prime minister's office responded to the news several days later, saying that the shift from US aid to partnership showed "the strength and sophistication" of the bilateral relationship.US military aid is less than 10% of Israel's annual military budget. But Yaakov Katz, author of several books about Israel's defence and security, said Trump's announcement was the tip of a much larger question around future funding, arms sales and joint military projects with Israel. All of this could be slowed or stalled by a Democrat-controlled Congress, even without the two-thirds majority it would need to overrule Trump."Everything that Israel used to get in a simpler, easier process will now potentially be much more complicated, and Israel has to be prepared that this is a new reality," he told me."Our entire Air Force is American-made military planes, we're dependent on American spare parts and American weapons. The last three years have shown us how dependent we are on American missile-defence systems. [If] those don't show up at the same pace, that's a real difference – that changes your calculation of what you're able to withstand if you go to war."Katz believes the midterms could also translate into tougher demands on Israel over its actions in Gaza and Lebanon, and a requirement not to undermine an agreement with Iran."Something will change in the US-Israeli relationship, but it's a question of scale," said the US official I spoke to, who was not authorized to speak on the record.  "It means shifting to [being] willing to criticise Israel when it's warranted, but the bedrock fundamental relationship will still be there."In an interview on Israeli television, the US ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee signalled little shift so far in core American positions, including on Israel's occupation of the West Bank, describing the sanctions imposed by other countries as "irrational" and counterproductive.Israel's ambassador to the UN, Danny Danon, told another Israeli channel that Trump would be in the White House for the next two years, and that Israel could "feel good" about the US veto in the UN Security Council – something Washington has repeatedly used in the past to block resolutions that target Israel."But we have to pay attention to the voices – not only in the Democratic Party but also the Republican Party – criticising Israel," he said. "It will be harder for us."Questions over its key alliance have come at a particularly sensitive time for Israel, less than two weeks after its own parliamentary elections left neither government nor opposition with a clear majority. Discussions are now taking place with the country's president, who will decide whether Netanyahu or his centrist rival, Gadi Eisenkot, will get the first chance to form a governing coalition."Under my leadership, we will renew and deepen that [US] partnership, strengthen the bipartisan foundations that have long sustained it," Eisenkot said in a social media post.Another member of his opposition bloc, Yair Lapid, said: "What do we do?""We go back to the rule that worked for us for seventy years, and which broke in 2015 when Netanyahu went to speak against [US president] Obama in Congress. Israel doesn't choose sides in America. We work with everyone."Netanyahu's speech to the US Congress in 2015 is seen as a defining moment in Israel's relationship with the US, when the Israeli leader appealed over the head of America's Democratic president to urge Republicans in Congress not to back a nuclear agreement with Iran.Since then, Netanyahu has increasingly anchored the alliance in Trump's Republican party, even as alienation among Democrats has grown.The US official I spoke to said that, before the midterms, Netanyahu could have improved the relationship with Washington by getting rid of his two far-right ministers."I think everyone understands now it's bigger than [that]," he said.How much the new tone in transatlantic relations will play into the task of building a new government in Israel is being closely watched.Some government supporters argue it has increased the need for political stability, and that Netanyahu provides much-needed continuity and a deep knowledge of the US and its leaders. "We cannot afford to be dragged into endless political disputes and election campaigns," said one opinion writer in Israel's largest-circulation daily, the right-wing Israel Hayom.Whoever heads Israel's next government, its American ally may demand more than rhetoric.In the noisy debate around what this will mean for Israel, the silence of its prime minister – once the whisperer of Washington's elite – is perhaps the most telling voice of all.

schema.headline: US midterm results spark fears in Israel over future of two countries' ties

title: How 2000s lad culture helped Russell Brand to hide in plain sight
description: Image source, Jo Hale/Getty ImagesImage caption, Russell Brand was found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assaultByCulture and m
body: Image source, Jo Hale/Getty ImagesImage caption, Russell Brand was found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assaultByCulture and media editorWarning: This article contains graphic descriptions of sexual actsNo British celebrity navigated the cultural changes of the early 21st Century better than Russell Brand.His life has been one long personal rebrand.He morphed from provocative stand-up comic to TV star and Hollywood actor. He became a YouTuber and political activist, taking up left-wing causes around issues of inequality in the 2010s, then Covid conspiracies and in 2024 supporting Donald Trump for president. That same year he was baptised as a Christian in London's River Thames.Now he has a new persona to try on: convicted rapist.On Thursday, the disgraced comedian was found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault at Southwark Crown Court, following a three-week trial.As he faces jail, it's clear that the behaviour that formed the backdrop to Brand's prosecution is the same behaviour that helped elevate him in the first place.Image source, Frank Micelotta/Getty Images for MTVImage caption, Brand performing at the MTV Video Music Awards a year after his memoir was publishedBrand shot to fame as a sexually outrageous libertine whose risque humour thrilled audiences.He cultivated the image of an insatiable, shameless womaniser. Sex, drugs and excess were central to his comic material.Over the decade of his offending, Brand sold out stand-up comedy venues and theatres, broadcasters - including MTV, Channel 4 and the BBC - started to throw money at him.With his backcombed hair and drainpipe black jeans, Brand regaled audiences at his stand-up comedy gigs with the graphic details of his sexual exploits: anal sex, prostitutes and orgies. He simulated masturbation and sex on stage. He said he liked oral sex with women "where it goes in their neck a little bit" and their "mascara runs a little bit," acting it out on stage.Even Brand's own barrister called the humour "a product of its time," reminding the jury in the trial that this graphic sexualised comedy was viewed as "radical and different" back then.Barely a generation later, many will view it as deeply rooted misogyny dressed up as humour. But these were different times.An era that celebrated casual sexismImage source, Press AssociationImage caption, Back then lads' magazines ruled - with their covers and double page spreads full of topless glamour models and half-naked female celebritiesThe late nineties and early noughties in Britain were an era that celebrated casual sexism and often elevated celebrities who espoused it. In 1999, FHM projected a naked photo of the Scottish TV presenter Gail Porter on to the Houses of Parliament. She only found out when she saw it on the news, and spoke later about how it deeply affected her mental health.What might now be termed toxic masculinity was often deemed funny, seen by some as good old-fashioned male humour. By others it was viewed as palatable because they believed it was being done with an apparently ironic eyebrow raise."There is no question he was a very talented stand-up," says Sarah Ditum, author of Toxic: Women, Fame and the Noughties. "There was an appetite for taboo breaking."I think it looks very old hat if you look back on that stuff. It's dated horribly and I don't think many people are going to be keen to defend Brand's act now knowing that it reflected his real world behaviour rather than an ironic performance."Image source, Jo Hale/Getty ImagesImage caption, My Booky Wook topped the Sunday Times bestseller chart for seven weeks in 2007But there were clues at the time that his outrageous stage act did not stop when the show ended - most publicly in his 2007 bestselling memoir, My Booky Wook."I'm a bloke from Grays with a good job and a terrific haircut who's been given a Wonka ticket to a lovely sex factory 'cos of ol' fame."Of course, many of his sexual partners consented. As his defence barrister told the jury "he devoted himself for many years to a highly promiscuous life", reminding them that "having lots of sex is completely lawful".My Booky Wook, which topped the Sunday Times bestseller chart for seven weeks in 2007 and sold 600,000 copies in hardback in the UK, opens with him checking into a clinic for sex addiction. He writes about going to lap dancing clubs and having "a lot" of oral sex in toilets and many threesomes.Fame and success brought him 'birds' "The rules change when you're famous. In that case two is often better than either none or one."He writes about how an MTV PR "reminded me that I put lap dances and prostitutes on her gold card and got the hotel to give me cash on her account without her prior knowledge".The Observer called it "a scandalous, libidinous memoir that is better written and more entertaining than any number of celebrity autobiographies that clog the shelves".Heat said: "You come away from the book feeling like you really know - and like - the real Russell."You can't imagine a celebrity these days writing a memoir in which he claims that at stage school a primetime actress, whom he names, "kissed me once in a corridor" and for years afterwards he'd tell people "'I had sex with her… And by sex, I mean bumming'".But it's all told in a jokey, revelatory way, by "a bloke from Essex who likes birds with big bottoms and big boobs…. Lovely dolly-birds".Image source, Don Arnold/WireImageImage caption, Meeting crowds backstage in Sydney in 2010 In light of his offending, writing that was celebrated for being frank, honest - and very funny - now looks anything but.People "are willing to mistake irony and self-awareness for truth telling and trustworthiness," says Ditum. "The idea that he made these jokes about being this kind of sexual monster was supposed to convince you that he wasn't actually a sexual monster in real life."Did normalising his behaviour allow him to hide in plain sight? Were the media companies who embraced him, the comedy venues who promoted him, the audiences who laughed at his humour, in some way complicit?A former TV boss who didn't want to be named explained the thinking of his peers like this: "You've got this charismatic presenter who appears to be very, very good and you don't want to lose that."The women who were being persecuted didn't feel empowered to speak up and the few who did feel empowered might have been classed as troublemakers but certainly weren't really listened to because you didn't want to lose the star. That was the process."Indeed, in Brand's trial, one of the complainants told the court she didn't report what had happened to her because she didn't think she would be believed in "those laddish culture times"."It was my word against his," she said in her evidence.'Brand was enabled'Jo Caulfield, a contemporary of Brand's on the early noughties stand-up circuit, says she initially found him "utterly charming" but she sees that he was "enabled and nobody will say anything against it"."People have people around them, promoters, assistants in TV. It's in the hierarchy of TV. If a runner [an entry-level production assistant] goes to his dressing room and he gets his knob out, it's like, 'oh, come on, don't make a fuss.'"And while safeguarding standards have been heavily tightened in some parts of the entertainment world, she says it "still goes on"."Nobody wants to upset the star. This person is making them money so everybody down the food chain better not say anything if they behave badly," says Caulfield.At the end of My Booky Wook, Brand writes "I have done some terrible things over the course of this booky wook… I mean, over my life."We now understand quite how terrible.

schema.headline: How 2000s lad culture helped Russell Brand to hide in plain sight

title: Russell Brand: Met Police boss 'wouldn't be surprised' if more allegations made about disgraced star
description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has also spoken about the case, seeking to explain the Labour Party's previous association with Brand, saying "it's not al
body: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has also spoken about the case, seeking to explain the Labour Party's previous association with Brand, saying "it's not always the case that people know everything about people in public life".Some within the party attempted to court Brand's support more than a decade ago, before police began investigating him.Ed Miliband, then the Labour leader, was interviewed by Brand in the run-up to the 2015 general election.In 2014, Burnham, then the shadow health secretary, posted in support of Brand on Twitter following allegations about the comedian's housing arrangements.It is not clear what Burnham had been referring to in his tweet, but the previous day, The Sun claimed Brand had paid rent at a property owned by a landlord in a tax haven, while at the same time campaigning against tax avoidance.Brand threatened to sue the newspaper and said he would give the money to victims of the Hillsborough disaster, a group Burnham has long campaigned with.In his 2014 tweet, Burnham said it was "depressing to see media mission to discredit someone who stops playing their game" and urged Brand to "keep going".Speaking on Friday, Burnham told the BBC: "His crimes are horrific, he's rightly been held to account, justice for the victims and that is the right course that's been taken here."All I can say is I had no idea of the full extent of what he was doing or what he went on to do."Speaking to the BBC on Friday, Sir Mark said that he "wouldn't be surprised if more people came forward" about Brand and said there were "two ongoing rape investigations" into him.Brand has already been interviewed under caution in relation to those allegations.In his interview Sir Mark praised the "bravery" of the women who came forward to tell "their story" to the police and during the trial."That's a real challenge for anyone having gone through something so ghastly and you have to admire them."The head of the Met also said that whilst Brand's case "may look different because it's about celebrity, the majority of sex offending is about people abusing power", adding that victims will be believed."We will do everything we can to bring to justice the powerful person who are responsible for probably the most ghastly moment in your life.", he said.It was put to Sir Mark during an interview with BBC Radio 4's Today programme that Brand's defence barrister "told jurors none of the complainants had in his words 'resisted, screamed or even tried to leave'".Sir Mark said that what he heard reported from the trial was "very close to victim blaming".Asked whether he would support the Victim's Commissioner's call for a legal duty in the Courts and Tribunals Bill that would require judges to direct juries on rape myths and misconceptions in every rape trial.He said he would "strongly support" that call, adding: "It shouldn't be possible for inaccurate statements to be made to a jury to suggest that because a rape victim didn't behave in one way that somehow undermines their case."Brand was refused bail following his conviction on Thursday and will now spend the weekend in custody before he is due to return to the same court on Monday for sentencing.He is expected to face a substantial prison sentence.Once the trial was over, it was reported that Brand is also facing further rape allegations made by two women and has already been questioned by officers in relation to the complaints. The Metropolitan Police said its investigation "remains ongoing".Details in legal documents from a hearing at London's Southwark Crown Court before Brand's criminal trial began suggest that one of the women was 16 years old at the time and featured in a Channel 4 documentary.The actor and comedian denied the allegations.None of the women who featured in the media investigation were the complainants from Brand's criminal trial.During a pre-trial hearing in October, Brand tried unsuccessfully to have his criminal case thrown out.His lawyers argued that the actor and entertainer could not receive a fair trial because of the publicity following the Dispatches programme.During the trial, Brand faced allegations from six women spanning the decade between 1999 and 2009, when he rose to fame as one of Britain's most high-profile entertainers.The women came to court to reveal how Brand used his immense fame to force them into sexual activity.The judge, Mr Justice Bennathan, told Brand to expect "a significant custodial term" after the verdicts were delivered.A man who was accused of laughing while Russell Brand sexually assaulted a woman in 2009, has been asked "to step back" from his employer while they consider the verdicts.Jack Bayles was part of his entourage in 2009 and was said to be present when one of the sexual assaults took place.Brand had been working on a Channel 4 project when he laid his head into the groin area of a woman who was helping him at the time.During the trial, the victim told the court Jack Bayles and another member of staff of Brand's had asked her to give the comedian a massage, and said he wouldn't continue unless she did. Shortly after - he sexually assaulted her.She had complained to her manager - who told the court through a statement at the trial that the victim had described how the men had laughed while the attack took place.In recent years, Jack Bayles has been working for the TV production company, Various Artists Ltd, as their head of comedy.In a statement, they told the BBC: "We have asked Jack Bayles to step back from the company whilst we consider the verdict and events surrounding the trial. Our thoughts, though, are primarily with every one of Brand's victims at this time."According to his biography on the Various Artists Ltd website, Bayles commissioned shows for Channel 4 including two series Derry Girls and Aisling Bea's This Way Up, plus Back, Year Of The Rabbit, Frank Of Ireland and Hullraisers.In a statement, Mr Bayles said he was sorry but doesn't remember the sexual assault."I am appalled and sickened by Brand's actions and have co-operated fully and voluntarily with the investigation and endeavoured to assist as best I can," he said. "However, I do not remember the incident that took place 17 years ago in 2009. But I acknowledge that I clearly missed something at the time and did not see nor recognise that it caused distress. For that I am sincerely sorry."He said at the time of the offence he was in the early stages of his career, calling it "a frantic, pressured and toxic working environment".He described Brand as someone who was "chaotic, dismissive and manipulated the people around him". The producer said this was why he decided to stop working with him in 2010, adding he "has not had any contact with him since", and that when he worked with him, no complaints were made to him about Brand's behaviour."I am unaware if any were raised to anyone else more senior to me," he said."I would never willingly or proactively wish to make anyone feel uncomfortable, unsafe or unsupported at work. If I was ever present when Brand acted inappropriately and I failed to spot it and step in, then I sincerely apologise".

schema.headline: Russell Brand: Met Police boss 'wouldn't be surprised' if more allegations made about disgraced star

title: Clicky Ponting scandal: Cricketer banned and Saltburn CC relegated
description: An amateur cricketer has been banned for two years for his role in the 'Clicky Ponting' cheating scandal that made headlines across the globe.Brian De
body: An amateur cricketer has been banned for two years for his role in the 'Clicky Ponting' cheating scandal that made headlines across the globe.Brian Devine, fielding at slip, clicked his fingers to mimic the noise of the ball taking the edge of the bat.Devine, playing for Saltburn second XI, was filmed in a North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League (NYSD) Division Two match against Norton in July.He has now been banned from all cricket under the jurisdiction of the England and Wales Cricket Board until 29 September 2028.Saltburn's second XI have also been relegated from Division Two and will start the 2027 season in Division Three with a 60-point deduction. The club has been fined £300.In a statement, the NYSD confirmed it has received complaints relating to the conduct of Devine and Saltburn in multiple matches.Both the player and the club admitted the charges. Devine accepted his punishment, while Saltburn appealed against theirs.Although Devine was the only player sanctioned, the NYSD was of the belief that other members of the Saltburn team were involved."In late July, the League received complaints about the alleged conduct of a Saltburn CC second XI player in NYSD Division Two matches and commenced an investigation with the co-operation of Saltburn CC," said the statement."The investigation ran over several weeks and included player interviews, written statements and a detailed review of video footage."In footage of the game between Saltburn and Norton, Devine appears to click his fingers as the ball passes Noman Shabir's bat before being caught by wicketkeeper Josh Bowes. Saltburn appeal and the umpire gives Shabir out.The clip went viral on social media, attracting media attention across the world.Now, following the investigation and disciplinary process, Devine is not permitted to play, coach, umpire, score or manage junior teams for the duration of his two-year ban.The relegation of Saltburn's second XI from Division Two means a reprieve for Middlesbrough's second XI after they finished 11th in the 12-team league.Saltburn's first XI had already been relegated from the NYSD Premier League following their 11th-place finish."The League recognises the strain this has placed on many people, especially those who were abused online and in person," added the NYSD. "We ask everyone to respect that the formal process is now complete."BBC Sport has contacted Saltburn CC and Devine for comment.

schema.headline: Clicky Ponting scandal: Cricketer banned and Saltburn CC relegated

title: Trump signs order to preserve Oval Office as national monument
description: US President Donald Trump has signed an executive order that he says will prevent future presidents from making certain changes to the White House Ova
body: US President Donald Trump has signed an executive order that he says will prevent future presidents from making certain changes to the White House Oval Office.The executive order declares the president's official office, which he has renovated, to be a national monument."We're making it a national monument, and it will not be allowed to be touched by anybody, destroyed, ripped down by stupid people, in order to build something in a slightly different shape," Trump told reporters on Thursday.The order does not prevent future presidents from changing the decor of the famous room.The document says that it does not "restrict the President's authority to redecorate the monument, select furnishings, or make ordinary operational and security modifications that do not substantially impair the monument's historic structure or architectural character".American presidents currently have the power to make some changes to the White House but large projects require the permission of Congress.The order comes months after Trump tore down the entirety of the White House East Wing in a project that has faced legal challenges.The project was not approved by the US Congress. Construction has continued, with plans to turn the space into a new ballroom. How Trump is remaking the White House in his own imageSigning the new executive order on Thursday, the president said: "We like the Oval Office, and it's a symbol, like the White House itself. It's a symbol of our country and the greatness of our country." He added that world leaders who have visited in recent months have complimented his decorative changes to the room.Trump said the White House and the Oval Office had been in need of repairs before his changes, calling it "badly damaged". He described broken windows, cracked walls and broken stone. Many of the noticeable changes, though, were cosmetic, including a large gold plaque reading "Oval Office" outside the space, paving over the Rose Garden and adding a new helicopter pad.Trump said the order would "make it impossible for anybody ever to destroy this incredible space".

schema.headline: Trump signs order to preserve Oval Office as national monument

title: Andy Burnham tells firms to publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law
description: Businesses should publish salaries in job adverts now, Prime Minister Andy Burnham is telling firms, rather than wait for a new law to come in that wi
body: Businesses should publish salaries in job adverts now, Prime Minister Andy Burnham is telling firms, rather than wait for a new law to come in that will force them to do so.The government is planning to make pay details compulsory in adverts, with legislation on the issue being brought forward "as soon as possible".It argues the change will help jobseekers, particularly those applying for their first job, and could help prevent pay discrimination. However, one industry group said setting pay was a complex process and regulating adverts was not always suitable.It comes a week after the UK's equality watchdog said employees should legally be able to find out what their colleagues are earning.Burnham said the current system felt "weighted against the applicant" and the changes were aimed at "tilting the scales back"."It can be quite soul destroying for young people these days, applying for jobs when the salary is not listed but sometimes they're not getting a reply," he told the BBC.The prime minister added that publishing salaries in adverts was also important for closing the gender pay gap.He was also challenged over whether MPs should be disclosing salaries when advertising for staff in their offices.A number of politicians are currently advertising for roles without giving an expected salary., externalBurnham said: "It would apply completely to them too and the call I'm making today is, before the law changes do it voluntarily because it's the right thing to do."The Cabinet Office launched a consultation into pay and reducing discrimination in the summer, and the government said there had been "overwhelming support" for greater transparency, with 94% of respondents backing the move."Whether you're a young person starting out or a parent trying to support your family, you should know what a job pays before spending your time and effort applying for it," Burnham said.The government said the move was part of attempts to reduce the nearly one million young people not in education, employment or training - or "Neet" - ahead of the final report of the Milburn Review into youth inactivity, which is due in the coming weeks.Publishing salary details upfront could "expose unjustified differences in pay, give workers greater confidence to challenge discrimination and prevent disagreements over pay escalating into disputes".The proposals are similar to measures being introduced in the European Union., externalEmployers in Europe will have to disclose the initial pay or range for new roles, which must either be included in a published job advert or shared before an interview.According to data from UK jobs website Adzuna, external, 51% of the adverts on its site in September had salary information, but the proportion has been falling in recent years.Adzuna co-founder Andrew Hunter said being open about pay "should be the norm, not the exception".He added that employers who put a salary on a job advert "attract more applicants, and better-suited ones".Previous research from the CIPD, external, an industry body for human resources managers, has indicated that the public sector and charities are more likely to reveal pay information that private firms, while pay ranges were more common than specific salaries.But it found not all employers were "fully transparent", with pay ranges sometimes wider than £10,000.CIPD chief executive Neil Carberry said that while, in principle, giving salary details was "a good thing", in practice it was "more complicated"."There isn't always a single fixed figure, and employers will want to set pay based on a candidate's skills, experience and potential."Carberry added the process was complex, saying that drafting job adverts is "best left to good employer practice rather than government regulation".The government has said it will set out further details on what information will be required and how the legislation will be enforced "in due course".Conservative shadow business secretary Julia Lopez said: "At a time when employers are finding it harder and harder to take on staff, Labour have decided to make their lives even more difficult."It should be up to businesses to decide what information they advertise about job openings, and to decide how to attract the best applicants. "As long as they are not being dishonest, misleading or discriminatory, it should not be a matter for the government."Last week, the Equality and Human Rights Commission (EHRC), said publishing salaries in job adverts would be a "positive step".It also said bosses should be required to respond to questionnaires about colleagues' pay to cut pay discrimination.At present, employers do not have to respond to employee requests for salary information about their co-workers.The EHRC also said employers should be prevented from asking about current salary when offering a job to stop a history of discrimination from continuing.Employers in the UK are currently allowed to ask you how much you get paid in your current role, but applicants are under no obligation to tell them.

schema.headline: Andy Burnham tells firms to publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law

title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments
description: Image source, Getty ImagesByEducation correspondentSeveral universities in England have only been using below-average salaries in examples of student
body: Image source, Getty ImagesByEducation correspondentSeveral universities in England have only been using below-average salaries in examples of student loan repayments on their websites, the BBC has found.Treasury Committee chair Dame Meg Hillier, who led a recent inquiry into student loans, said some information about repayments was "misleading", including one instance where they were compared to the "cost of a daily coffee".She also said the Department for Education (DfE) must include higher-salary examples on its own website, too.The DfE said it would review the information it provides, while universities said their websites referred to government information and would be reviewed where necessary.Student loan repayments are tied to earnings, so the more you earn, the more you repay every month - and graduates generally go on to earn more than non-graduates.Current and prospective students in England take out Plan 5 loans to pay for their tuition fees and living costs. They repay 9% of anything they earn over £25,000 for 40 years, or until the loan is paid off.The BBC looked at publicly available information on more than 110 university websites in England and found cases of inaccurate information about the salary at which they start repaying and the length of time they repay for.It also found that 12 universities only gave students worked examples of repayments based on earnings that are less than the UK average, which is £39,039.The University of Gloucestershire website, for example, specified a £26,000 salary would mean repaying £7.47 per month, while Northumbria University and the University of Huddersfield gave examples of £75 monthly repayments based on a £35,000 salary. Northumbria University's website said those graduates would be "repaying an amount less than the cost of a daily coffee" - a comparison that has been removed since the university was contacted by the BBC.The DfE website also only gives examples of monthly repayments for people earning up to £38,400 on other student loan plans, but does not include any real-world repayment examples for Plan 5 students.Repayments are 9% of earnings over £25,000, so someone earning £30,000 will repay £37.50 per month, but someone earning £100,000 will repay £562.50 per month. Megan Russon, 21, is a recently graduated tax accountant from Cannock with a starting salary of around £29,000, meaning she will repay about £30 a month.However, she expects to earn around £50,000 when she becomes chartered in three years' time, and will be repaying about £187 per month.Image source, Megan RussonImage caption, Megan owes about £62,000 after graduating from the University of Birmingham with a degree in accounting and financeMegan says universities gave examples of repayments based on earnings of between £25,000 and £45,000 at open days and said graduates "wouldn't even notice the repayments because they should be minimal"."At the time, I wasn't sure what salary I was even going to be on when I graduated," she said. "When I was at university, I started realising the salaries that I was going to be on after I graduated, then I started realising actually this is going to be impacting me quite a lot."The BBC's analysis found most university websites did not give worked examples, and most also referred to DfE, Student Loans Company or Student Finance England information whether they did or not. More than a dozen provided examples of repayments based on higher-than-average earnings, but 12 gave examples that were lower:University of Gloucestershire (repaying £7.50 per month)University of Birmingham (repaying £22 per month)London South Bank University (repaying £22.50 per month)Manchester Metropolitan University (repaying £33 per month)Birmingham City University, Open University, the University of Sheffield, and the University of Wolverhampton (repaying £37.50 per month)University of Portsmouth (repaying £45 per month)Birkbeck University (repaying £54 per month)Northumbria University and University of Huddersfield (repaying £75 per month)There were also instances of inaccurate information. The University of Exeter said Plan 5 loans were written off a decade earlier than they actually are, Royal Holloway and Edge Hill listed the wrong repayment thresholds, and Harper Adams said students from England were still on Plan 2 loans. All four universities have updated their websites since being contacted by the BBC."I'm pretty shocked at what the BBC has uncovered here and I'm going to be raising it with the relevant MPs and urging them to write to the universities in their constituencies to make them step up and do a better job," Dame Meg said.She said the DfE should be "taking the lead" by reflecting repayments for higher earners, but that universities also "have a responsibility to the young people that they're taking on board for the three or four years of their degree".Will we ever pay back our student loans?England's controversial student loans system has left many graduates frustrated.Dame Meg chaired an inquiry into student loans this year and said the DfE had been "mis-selling" Plan 2 loans, which were given between 2012 and 2023 in England and are still issued in Wales.Her report said the DfE had not made clear how higher earnings would affect monthly repayments and criticised comparisons to £30-a-month phone contracts.The DfE then pledged to "improve the current information that is provided to prospective borrowers" including "the impact of salary progression" on monthly repayments.Lewis Wilson, from the National Union of Students, said the BBC's findings were "shocking", adding: "Students should be able to rely upon information from their universities and if this was any other financial product, it would have crossed the line into mis-selling."The DfE said its guidance sets out "how repayments are calculated across the different repayment plans", adding that it was "vital" that university applicants have "clear and accurate information"."We have committed to reviewing the information we provide following the Treasury Committee's recommendations, and we will. We are also working with universities to ensure the information they provide to students is clear and up to date," it added.The University of Gloucestershire, the University of Birmingham and Harper Adams University said they had updated their websites and Birkbeck, University of London said it was reviewing the information.The University of Sheffield said its example was illustrative, while Manchester Metropolitan University and the University of Wolverhampton said examples were explanatory and would be reviewed. London South Bank University said it regularly reviews content on its website to ensure it is helpful and accurate.The Open University said it gave examples of "income levels that are most likely to reflect our students' circumstances", although many students "go on to earn significantly more", while the University of Portsmouth said its example was taken from Student Finance England and would be updated to "reflect the most recent average salary".Northumbria University said its example of £35,000 was "broadly in line with the average for full-time workers in the North East of England" but added: "We recognise that higher earners will make higher monthly repayments and will further review all pages to make sure the wording is as clear and precise as possible."Birmingham City University declined to comment. The BBC has requested a comment from the University of Huddersfield.Get in touchAre your student loan repayments particularly high?Get our flagship newsletter with all the headlines you need to start the day. Sign up here.

schema.headline: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

title: England squad news: Thomas Tuchel says Cole Palmer misses 'too many chances to impress' after not selecting Chelsea forward
description: Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Thomas Tuchel has named three uncapped players in his England squadByMike PeterBBC Sport journalistEngland ma
body: Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Thomas Tuchel has named three uncapped players in his England squadByMike PeterBBC Sport journalistEngland manager Thomas Tuchel said Cole Palmer "misses too many chances to impress" after not selecting the Chelsea forward for November's Nations League fixtures.Palmer, 24, dropped out of England's squad for their previous games in early autumn and is absent again for matches against Croatia at Wembley on Thursday, 12 November and Spain in Madrid on Sunday, 15 November.Tuchel has instead handed Fulham's Josh King and Borussia Dortmund's Jobe Bellingham their first England call-ups. Both players are attacking midfielders."We have enough number 10s and we stick to the guys who were in the previous camp because we were happy with the two and a half weeks we had together," said Tuchel."We have Josh King as a new player in there, but I want to see him on both wings. He is kind of an extra player and he can play all four positions."I guess everyone is desperate to play for England and Cole is no exception. "We are speaking now about a player that is not in camp. It counts when you are in camp and I just said last time that he misses too many opportunities to impress."Jobe, 21, joins his brother Jude in the England squad - and they could be the first pair of siblings to feature in an England line-up since Gary and Phil Neville.England sit second behind Spain in group A3 of the Nations League with three wins and a loss.One more point from their remaining two matches will secure a place in the two-legged quarter-finals in March, with the winners of those ties advancing to the Nations League Finals in June.England squad for Croatia and Spain matchesGoalkeepers: Jordan Pickford (Everton), Jason Steele (Brighton & Hove Albion), James Trafford (Leeds United)Defenders: Trent Alexander-Arnold (Real Madrid), Jarrad Branthwaite (Everton), Marc Guehi (Manchester City), Lewis Hall (Newcastle United), Ezri Konsa (Arsenal), Jarell Quansah (Bayer Leverkusen), Djed Spence (Inter Milan), Ben White (Arsenal)Midfielders: Elliot Anderson (Manchester City), Jobe Bellingham (Borussia Dortmund), Jude Bellingham (Real Madrid), James Garner (Everton), Josh King (Fulham), Myles Lewis-Skelly (Arsenal), Declan Rice (Arsenal)Forwards: Dominic Calvert-Lewin (Leeds United), Eberechi Eze (Arsenal), Morgan Gibbs-White (Nottingham Forest), Anthony Gordon (Barcelona), Harry Kane (Bayern Munich), Rio Ngumoha (Liverpool), Morgan Rogers (Chelsea)'Standout' Bellingham and 'flexible' KingThe selection of Jobe Bellingham for the senior squad means he continues to follow in the footsteps of his older brother.Both graduates of the Birmingham City academy, the brothers were regular selections in England youth line-ups.Jobe joined Dortmund from Sunderland in summer 2025 in a deal worth up to £31m, having helped the Wearside club win promotion to the Premier League via the play-offs. The move mirrored one made by Jude, 23, who played for the German side between 2020 and 2023 before signing for Real Madrid.Tuchel said England Under-21 coach Lee Carsley had been "speaking very highly" of Jobe Bellingham "for a while"."He is the captain of the under-21s so I think the door should always be open and the pathway should always be open for special performances over a long period of time and that is what Jobe has done," he added."He found his way and his rhythm with Dortmund, where he has had an excellent start to the season. He is a regular starter there and now very influential."Bellingham has been preferred to Kobbie Mainoo, with Tuchel saying the Manchester United midfielder, who was an early withdrawal from the last squad, has had a "difficult spell with his club"."The door is always open for younger players to overtake and make their mark," he added.King has had a strong start to the Premier League season, scoring two goals and making one assist, and has played at every youth level for England.The 19-year-old Fulham academy graduate has scored one goal in nine appearances for England Under-21s, and Tuchel called him "a fantastic character" who "gives us a bit of flexibility"."We decided to nominate 22 outfield players for flexibility in training and he is the extra player in training, if you will," Tuchel added.Figure caption, 'Palmer misses too many opportunities to impress' - TuchelWhat other changes are there?Arsenal forward Bukayo Saka misses out on the November fixtures after sustaining a quadriceps injury against Bayern Munich last month.The Premier League champions believe the 25-year-old will be absent for six weeks after he was substituted early in the Champions League game against Bayern Munich.Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott is also not selected after picking up an injury against Croatia in October.The 23-year-old, who made his England debut in the first international break of the season and was described as "the complete package" by Tuchel, is reportedly in contention to return for the Cherries against Ipswich on Sunday.Manchester United's Marcus Rashford and Newcastle's Tino Livramento, who both pulled out the last squad prior to any matches being played, also miss out with respective hip and knee injuries.Como's Trevoh Chalobah is another absentee, while Manchester City's Nico O'Reilly and Rico Lewis have also not been selected.James Garner of Everton and Nottingham Forest's Morgan Gibbs-White retain their places after being added to England's last squad prior to any fixtures being played, while Arsenal's Ben White and Inter Milan's Djed Spence return for the first time since the summer.The Arsenal pair of Declan Rice and Ezri Konsa, who both withdrew from the last England party, are fit and selected.

schema.headline: England squad news: Thomas Tuchel says Cole Palmer misses 'too many chances to impress' after not selecting Chelsea forward

title: England v Australia: Fin Smith fit to face Wallabies
description: Fly-half Fin Smith has recovered from a calf injury and will start for England in their opening Test of the autumn against Australia on Sunday.Smith h
body: Fly-half Fin Smith has recovered from a calf injury and will start for England in their opening Test of the autumn against Australia on Sunday.Smith has started England's past five matches at 10, but was a doubt to face the Wallabies in the Nations Championship encounter after coming off late on in Northampton's defeat by Leicester on 24 October.The 24-year-old is joined in the England XV by flanker Ben Curry, who makes his Test return after an injury-hit 16 months.Curry, whose twin brother Tom had an injury setback in training earlier this week that took him out of contention, is seen as key to combating Australia's breakdown specialists Fraser McReight and Carlo Tizzano and ensuring a supply of quick ball to Smith and his backline.Smith will have Saints team-mate Tommy Freeman as an attacking outlet and a target for crossfield kicks on the wing, while full-back George Furbank, who can step in at first receiver, played alongside both before his summer move to Harlequins.Alex Coles, another Northampton player, wins a starting second-row spot ahead of George Martin, while Henry Slade is chosen at outside centre, with no space for either Joe Marchant or Will Joseph in the matchday 23.Fin Baxter, who only made two appearances since a comeback from a 10-month foot-injury lay-off, is the starting loose-head prop, with Ellis Genge poised on the bench alongside Will Stuart, another welcome front-row returnee.Borthwick will hope Plymouth-born Exeter star Fisilau, who was first called up to the senior squad in January and whose father Keni represented Tonga, can bring some of the heavy-duty ball carrying lost by Tom Willis' departure to French club rugby."[Fisilau has] worked incredibly hard to get to this point and has earned his opportunity through the way he's performed for Exeter and in our training environment," said Borthwick."He's a powerful, athletic player who brings real energy to the team."England are playing at Twickenham's Allianz Stadium for the first time since February's 42-21 defeat by Ireland and are in need of a strong campaign to propel them towards next year's Six Nations and Rugby World Cup.England XV: Furbank; Freeman, Slade, Atkinson, Feyi-Waboso; F Smith, van Poortvliet; Baxter, George, Heyes, Itoje, Coles, Chessum, Curry, EarlReplacements: Cowan-Dickie, Genge, Stuart, Martin, Fisilau, Pollock, Spencer, M SmithAustralia have named Jeremy Williams, more usually a second row, at blindside flanker as they target England's set-piece.Elsewhere Len Ikitau, who spent last season at Exeter, returns at inside centre after missing the defeat by New Zealand under the head injury assessment protocols.Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii, who enjoyed a winning Test debut in this fixture two years ago, is named on the wing, while there is plenty of power on the bench to take on England's replacements with Rob Valentini, Taniela Tupou and Carlo Tizzano biding their time on the sidelines.Australia: Wright; Jorgensen, Suaalii, Henry, Ikitau; Meredith, Lonergan; Bell, Pollard, Alaalatoa, Canham, Salakaia-Loto, Williams, McReight, WilsonReplacements: Nasser, Kailea, Tupou, Valetini, Tizzano, McDermott, Donaldson, Daugunu

title: Jude and Jobe Bellingham: 'Incredible achievement' as brothers called up to England squad
description: Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Jude and Jobe Bellingham could be the first brothers to play together for England since Gary and Phil Neville
body: Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Jude and Jobe Bellingham could be the first brothers to play together for England since Gary and Phil Neville 19 years agoByEngland reporterIt may be a surprise to some but Jobe Bellingham's call-up to the England senior side has been a long time coming.The 21-year-old’s career path has been very similar to that of his older brother Jude - England's star player at the World Cup and one of Real Madrid's best players. Both were stars of the Birmingham City academy before big-money moves to the German Bundesliga and England call-ups.Jobe's debut for Birmingham came at the age of 16 years and 107 days - 69 days older than Jude when he made his first appearance for the Blues' senior side.The central midfielder then moved to Sunderland and helped them win promotion to the Premier League before joining German side Borussia Dortmund at the age of 19 in a deal worth up to £31m. Jude also moved to Dortmund when he was 17, before developing into one of the world's best players and joining Real Madrid.Having one of the best midfielders in the world as your older brother comes with challenges and Jobe has consistently been compared to his sibling. But the former Sunderland midfielder is his own player, wearing 'Jobe' on the back of his shirt instead of his family name. He said it was suggested to him by a former coach because "it shows that I'm going my own way".Jobe is a different type of player to Jude, sitting deeper in the midfield, but is as physically imposing while still being good on the ball.He is the current captain of the England Under-21 side, and England manager Thomas Tuchel said Young Lions head coach Lee Carsley had been pushing for some time for the younger Bellingham to get senior recognition. "He's the standout player," said Tuchel. "He's the captain, so the door should always be open for the pathway, always be open for special performances over a long period of time."That's what Jobe has done on top of it. He found his way, he found his rhythm with Dortmund. He's had an excellent start to his season, is a regular starter and influential." Figure caption, Thomas Tuchel on Jobe Bellingham's England call-upEngland host Croatia at Wembley on Thursday, 12 November before travelling  to Madrid to take on Spain on 15 November in this next international break.With Arsenal's Myles Lewis-Skelly suspended for the first game, and Bournemouth's Alex Scott out injured after shining on his debut in last month's 7-0 win over Croatia, Tuchel said a natural "opportunity" for Jobe had opened up. "He deserves to make an impression for us," said the German in his news conference after naming the squad."It's an incredible achievement for the family and for the brothers. I saw his excitement straight away and his smile. "He has an open and calm personality. He's one of five players for the central midfield. "He's a more defensive player than Jude. So strong on the ball, good physique, a big body, a very physical player and can keep possession. "It's now up to him, but he's excited and happy and eager to impress, and that's the best foundation to have a good camp for him."Image source, Jude Bellingham InstagramImage caption, Jude shared a throwback photo of him and Jobe after Friday's squad announcementWhich other brothers have played for England?If they get on the pitch together, Jude and Jobe won't be the first brothers to represent the Three Lions.It has been 19 years since Gary and Phil Neville, who both played for Manchester United, last played together for England, and 30 years since they started.They first played together for England in 1996 against China, becoming the first siblings to do so since Bobby and Jack Charlton 26 years earlier.Jack and Bobby were both part of England's 1966 World Cup-winning squad.Bobby was the younger of the two, but made his Three Lions debut first. He went on to win 106 international caps.Jack, who was not called into the England team until days before his 30th birthday, won 35 caps.More recently, brothers Nathaniel and Trevoh Chalobah have both played for England, but never alongside each other.Nathaniel made his solitary appearance as an injury-time substitute in a 3-2 away win against Spain in a 2018 Nations League game.His younger brother Trevoh, currently a Como defender, made the first of his three international appearances against Senegal in June 2025 and was in England's 2026 World Cup squad.Image gallerySkip image galleryImage source, Getty ImagesImage caption, The Nevilles played 31 times for EnglandSlide 1 of 3, Phil and Gary Neville, The Nevilles played 31 times for England'Jobe has shown remarkable progress'Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Jobe Bellingham has made 14 appearances for Dortmund this seasonByConstantin EcknerGerman Football WriterJobe has shown remarkable progress since last winter. In the first couple of months, following his move from Sunderland to Borussia Dortmund, he seemed timid, as if he was just trying to avoid making any mistakes. His passes rarely, if ever, caused trouble for opposing defences.Even Dortmund manager Niko Kovac said at one point that he was surprised how long it might take him to get comfortable in the Bundesliga. But hard work in the gym to build up muscle mass in order to become more explosive and the fact that he received plenty of chances in Dortmund's line-up has helped his development.In the latter stages of last season, his decision-making was much faster and his intensity seemed higher. Still, Dortmund decided to sign Dutch midfielder Joey Veerman, a specialist at making line-breaking passes, in August. It meant Jobe's place in the starting XI was far from secure at the beginning of this season.In recent games, Kovac has employed Bellingham in a more advanced role, as one of the two number 10s behind the striker. In this role, Bellingham drove into the final third with pace and showed intensity during pressing sequences. His performance in the 2-2 draw against Bayern Munich in the Bundesliga last Saturday was arguably his best since his arrival in Germany.
